In 2027, it does. Thousands of pilgrims will walk here this year.
Is 2027 your Camino year?
A Holy Year doesn't come every 5 years. Or every 10. Here's why it's 2027.
One: it only happens when July 25 falls on a Sunday.
Two: that's why it follows an odd rhythm: every 6, 5, 6 and 11 years.
Three: the last one lasted two years, 2021 and 2022, because of the pandemic.
Four: after 2027, the next one isn't until 2032.
Which one surprised you? Tell me in the comments.
Only have a week off? Pick one of these 4 Caminos.
One: the French Way from Sarria. The classic, and the liveliest.
Two: the English Way from Ferrol. Estuaries, harbours and very few people.
Three: Santiago to Finisterre. It ends at the sea, where the world once ended.
Four: the Primitive Way from Lugo. The oldest Camino, through inland Galicia.
Comment your number and we'll tell you more.
Walking the Camino from Sarria? These are its 5 stages.
Sarria to Portomarín: 14 miles of villages and country lanes.
Portomarín to Palas de Rei, with gentle climbs and small villages.
Palas de Rei to Arzúa, the longest. If you like, split it with a night in Melide.
Arzúa to A Rúa, through woods and hamlets.
And A Rúa to Santiago, all the way to the Cathedral.
69 miles and your Compostela. Save this for your Camino.
